echo-samples.title: Same echo, louder here, quieter there
echo-samples.caption: The echo is half a copy of each tone, 4 samples late. For 2,000 Hz it lands on top of the tone; for 1,000 Hz it pulls against it.

gain-ripple.title: The echo’s gain ripples
gain-ripple.caption: The gain of the 4-sample echo at every tone from 0 to 4,000 Hz, with the six values from the table as dots. It peaks every 2,000 Hz.

echo-wheel.title: The echo arrow swings round
echo-wheel.caption: At each tone the echo arrow sits 4 per-sample steps behind the original: 90° at 500 Hz, 180° at 1,000 Hz, a full lap at 2,000 Hz. The sum arrow’s length is the gain.

delay-vs-ripple.title: A longer delay makes a finer ripple
delay-vs-ripple.caption: Two wide humps against twenty narrow ones. Ten times the delay, a ripple ten times tighter.

log-spectrum.title: The log makes the ripple the same height
log-spectrum.caption: Top: the echo’s ripple is huge on the voice’s hump and invisible in its valley. Bottom: after the log, the same ripple has the same height everywhere.

tone-circle.title: Sixteen tones round the circle
tone-circle.caption: The echo’s gain is sampled at these 16 tones: no voice, no recording. Each tone below the line mirrors one above it and has the same gain.

list-dft.title: The list’s FFT lights up bin 4
list-dft.caption: The list repeats every 4 bins, so it goes round 4 times across all 16, and the FFT lights up bin 4: the delay. Bin 12 is its mirror.

lapping-echo.title: The echo laps the tone D times
lapping-echo.caption: Once round the circle, the 4-sample echo laps the tone 4 times, so the log ripple has 4 bumps and the match lands on bin 4.

cepstrum.title: The cepstrum: a spectrum of a spectrum
cepstrum.caption: The recipe at a glance.

bins-vs-ripple.title: The record must hold more than 2D samples
bins-vs-ripple.caption: More than two bins per ripple, or the peak lands at a false quefrency: 176 and 848 for records too short, 1,200 for 8,192 samples.

real-cepstrum.title: The cepstrum of the real call
real-cepstrum.caption: Everything below 100 is the voice’s shape; the bumps at 64 and its multiples are its pitch. Beyond that, the tallest peak is the echo, with its dip at twice the delay.

lopsided-log.title: The lopsided ripple
lopsided-log.caption: The log squashes the peaks and stretches the dips. Describing that lopsided ripple takes cosines at two and three times the speed: the smaller spikes at 2D and 3D.

canceller.title: Two cancellers
canceller.caption: Subtract a shifted copy of heard and the echo’s own echo is left, −0.25 at 2D. Subtract a shifted copy of clean and nothing is left.
